*   **Provider:** Dr. Okafor, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

Dear Appeals Committee,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for my scheduled total ankle replacement (CPT 27702), to be performed by Dr. Okafor. The denial letter dated August 14, 2026, states that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." 

This determination is inconsistent with my actual clinical history and the criteria set forth in your plan’s governing Clinical UM Guideline, **CG-SURG-74 ("Total Ankle Replacement")**. 

Your medical policy, **CG-SURG-74**, states that:
> "Total ankle replacement using a U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved device... is considered medically necessary to replace a painful arthritic ankle joint due to osteoarthritis, post-traumatic arthritis, or rheumatoid arthritis when criteria in A, B, and C below are met:"

Below, we demonstrate how my clinical records explicitly satisfy each of these medical-necessity requirements, with particular focus on the conservative treatment timeline.

### 1. Group A: Clinical Features & Failed Conservative Treatment
Under Group A, your policy requires that the patient is a:
> "Skeletally mature individual; and"

And exhibits:
> "Ankle pain that significantly limits daily activity; and"

Furthermore, the policy mandates the:
> "Completion and failure of at least 6 months of conservative treatment (such as anti-inflammatory medication, physical therapy, splints or orthotic devices as indicated); AND"

My medical records document **18 months of progressive, severe ankle pain** that significantly limits my daily activities. I suffer from an antalgic gait and my mobility is restricted to ambulating only two blocks. 

More importantly, my trial of conservative care far exceeds the "at least 6 months" threshold and has unequivocally failed:
*   **Supervised Physical Therapy:** I completed a highly structured, 16-week course of supervised physical therapy focusing on ankle strengthening and balance. This course spanned from March 24, 2026, to July 14, 2026, comprising 20 total visits, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
*   **Oral Medications:** I tried a continuous 4-month course of oral NSAIDs, which failed to provide adequate pain relief. 
*   **Interventional Injections:** I received a therapeutic corticosteroid injection on May 5, 2026, which yielded only 3 weeks of partial, temporary relief before my severe symptoms returned.

When combining my 18 months of persistent pain with 4 months of NSAID therapy, a steroid injection, and nearly 4 months of intensive physical therapy, my conservative management trial spans well over the required 6-month window. 

### 2. Group B: Associated Clinical Conditions
Under Group B, the policy requires that:
> "At least 1 of the following clinical conditions are present:
> • Arthritis in adjacent joints (that is, subtalar or midfoot); or
> • Arthrodesis of the contralateral ankle; or
> • Inflammatory (for example, rheumatoid) arthritis; or
> • Severe arthritis of the contralateral ankle; AND"

To satisfy this requirement, my clinical files show that I meet the following condition(s): **[Specify which Group B criterion is met: e.g., arthritis in adjacent subtalar or midfoot joints / previous contralateral ankle arthrodesis / inflammatory (rheumatoid) arthritis / severe contralateral ankle arthritis]**. Weight-bearing radiographs taken on July 17, 2026, confirm severe tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts.

### 3. Group C: Exclusionary Criteria / Contraindications
Under Group C, the policy requires that:
> "None of the following contraindications to total ankle replacement are present: Active ankle joint infection · Charcot neuropathy · Compromised bone stock or soft tissue · Extensive avascular necrosis of the talar dome · Malalignment (such as varus or valgus deformity greater than 15 degrees) not correctable by surgery · Peripheral vascular disease"

My pre-operative evaluation by Dr. Okafor confirms the complete absence of these contraindications:
*   There is no active ankle joint infection.
*   There is no Charcot neuropathy.
*   I have stable bone stock and soft tissue.
*   My BMI is 29, I am a non-smoker, and there is no active or untreated substance use.
*   **[Confirm absence of extensive avascular necrosis, uncorrectable malalignment > 15 degrees, and peripheral vascular disease]**.

### Conclusion
My clinical history documents 18 months of debilitating pain, severe radiographic joint space obliteration, and a exhaustive, multi-modality trial of conservative care (including physical therapy, NSAIDs, and injections) lasting over 6 months that has failed to restore my function. 

I meet all medical-necessity criteria under Clinical UM Guideline **CG-SURG-74**. I request that you review the attached clinical records—specifically the physical therapy discharge note from July 2026, the pre-operative surgical notes from Dr. Okafor, and my July 17, 2026 radiographs—and immediately reverse this denial.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Quinn Iverson
